rationale: The author's seeded defect (one-stage synchroniser, CDC-005) is absent: stage_one -> data_o_r[0] is a clean depth-2 clk_b chain (line 9), with constant padding only and no early tap. CDC-005 cannot trigger, since it needs depth >= 2 and below min_stages=2. Both readers labelled this case good. I settle on unknown instead. src_a[0] follows data_i[0] every clk_a cycle (input delay on clk_a), at the same period as clk_b, so source levels can be skipped. The RTL gives no hold or stability guarantee, and no statement that sample loss is tolerable. CDC-013(a) (source period < 1.5x destination) discloses exactly this rate obligation (WARNING). Labelling the case good would claim a safety that the evidence does not establish. Raw rst_n release, recovery/removal and physical timing remain external obligations outside this label.
